headline: ShinyHunters says an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day handed it records on every FBI employee, while attackers worked live exploits in Check Point, Arista, and Zyxel gear.

emerging_trends.text: One Chinese-speaking crew works both ends of the stack, pulling government data off 996 Zyxel switches and more than 18,500 records out of WordPress backend databases, which puts cheap network hardware and ordinary content management systems inside the same intrusion.

Attackers keep handing the thinking to models: CLOSEDQUORUM asks Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral what to do next inside a compromised Windows host, and the EvilTokens phishing service leaned on AI at every step of its chain.

emerging_trends.text: The management plane draws the fire now, with attackers running scripts on Check Point Security Management Servers and exploiting Arista's VeloCloud Orchestrator, each a box that dictates policy to every firewall or SD-WAN edge beneath it.

topics.title: CLOSEDQUORUM Runs Its Own Command and Control
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos released CAIRN, a research toolkit that classifies AI-integrated malware entirely from file metadata such as submitter, import hash, domain, and AI provider, with no download and no detonation, and used it on September 22, 2026 to surface CLOSEDQUORUM, a Windows binary that drives its entire command and control loop through AI chatbots with no operator involvement; BleepingComputer named the four models it queries for post-compromise decisions, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral.
topics.summary: CLOSEDQUORUM is the first reported implant that decides its own next actions through a language model instead of waiting on a human handler, which moves large stretches of the attack chain off the attacker's keyboard. Talos published CAIRN so defenders can hunt for the same pattern in their own telemetry.

topics.title: Chinese-Speaking Crew Loots 996 Zyxel Switches
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer widened the picture on September 22, 2026: the same Chinese-speaking actor GreyNoise caught exploiting CVE-2026-7273 across 996 Zyxel GS1900 switches in 48 countries also exploits WordPress flaws, and has pulled more than 18,500 records out of backend databases holding government data, one day after CISA cataloged the switch flaw with a federal patch deadline of Thursday, September 24, 2026.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-7273 is a stack-based buffer overflow rated 8.8 in the Zyxel GS1900 line of Gigabit Ethernet switches that yields arbitrary operating system command execution; the compromised devices sit mostly in Italy, the United States, Taiwan, South Korea, and other European Union countries. Zyxel has shipped fixes, and CISA cataloged a Veeam flaw granting SYSTEM access alongside it.

topics.title: WordPress Core Yields Two Paths to Server Code
topics.latest_developments: WordPress shipped version 7.1.2 on September 22, 2026 for a third core flaw, this one letting an attacker with no account make a site load a PHP file from outside its theme folders and, on some servers, run their own code, and backported the fix to every branch the project still supports, back to 4.7; researchers published a working proof-of-concept for Click2Shell the day before.
topics.summary: Click2Shell is a cross-site request forgery bug in WordPress core that installs and previews a theme when a logged-in administrator opens a crafted link, ending in remote code execution; Comment2Shell, CVE-2026-93485, lets an anonymous visitor leave a comment carrying a hidden script that runs code on the server once an administrator views the page. Site owners should move to WordPress 7.1.2 now.

topics.title: VeloCloud Orchestrator and D-Link Routers Under Fire
topics.latest_developments: CISA put CVE-2026-93952, the 10.0-rated improper input validation flaw Arista disclosed in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator, into its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 22, 2026 alongside CVE-2026-94127, a heap-based buffer overflow in F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager; D-Link warned the same day of CVE-2026-86296, a maximum-severity zero-day in legacy DIR-822A dual-band Wi-Fi routers that carries public proof-of-concept code and no patch, and Dinh Ho Anh Khoa of Viettel Cyber Security showed that CVE-2026-65660, which Microsoft first filed as a 6.5 spoofing bug, gives an authenticated user remote code execution on SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition.
topics.summary: VeloCloud Orchestrator manages the Edge devices in a VeloCloud SD-WAN, and only orchestrators that authenticate their Edges with certificates carry the flaw. Microsoft has shipped SharePoint patches, D-Link owners of DIR-822A hardware have no fix and should retire the devices.

topics.title: EvilTokens Phishing Service Falls to Microsoft
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit seized 50 websites and disabled more than 150 domains on September 22, 2026 under an order from the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, working with Health-ISAC, Cloudflare, Coinbase, OpenAI, Railway, SpyCloud, and the Shadowserver Foundation, after EvilTokens compromised more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts at over 10,000 organizations; police in the United Kingdom arrested two people.
topics.summary: EvilTokens sold device code phishing on Telegram for a $1,500 initiation fee plus $500 a month, pairing AI-written lures and automated infrastructure with token theft that walks past passwords, then helping buyers mine the stolen inboxes for fraud. Organizations should block device code authentication flows they do not use and hunt for unfamiliar token grants.

topics.title: Malicious npm Packages Steal Credentials and Repositories
topics.latest_developments: Checkmarx detailed indexed-btree on September 22, 2026, a package that impersonates the legitimate sorted-btree indexing utility, hides its loader in a prototype method inside ordinary runtime code to dodge install-script defenses, and collected millions of downloads before npm pulled it; The Hacker News described a second package, tw-pkgprobe-7731, which the npm account twdepprobe7731 uploaded in mid-August 2026 posing as a Twilio bug-bounty security tool while harvesting credentials, and Dark Reading traced CrowdSec's loss of 170 private GitHub repositories to an OAuth token the Shai-Hulud worm lifted from a former employee's computer through the TanStack npm compromise.
topics.summary: Attackers now bury malicious logic in the code a package runs during normal use, which slips past the registry and enterprise controls built to inspect install scripts. Development teams should pin dependencies, review new packages that mimic popular utility names, and revoke OAuth tokens belonging to departed employees.

topics.title: Check Point Management Servers Face an Exploited Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Check Point Software shipped emergency hotfixes on September 22, 2026 and identified the flaw as CVE-2026-93616, a path traversal that lets anyone who reaches the Security Management Server's web service run scripts on it without logging in, which attackers used in a handful of targeted attacks on July 23, 2026; CISA added that flaw and CVE-2026-85102, an improper certificate validation bug in multiple Check Point products, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day.
topics.summary: A Security Management Server holds the policy, logs, and credentials for an organization's entire Check Point firewall fleet, so code execution there reaches every gateway it manages. Administrators should install the hotfix immediately and review management server logs for unexplained script execution.

topics.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops a Defender Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Abdelhamid Naceri, a former employee of Microsoft Germany, revealed that they are the exploit leaker known as Nightmare Eclipse and Chaotic Eclipse, and published the tool behind the latest Microsoft Defender zero-day on GitHub on September 19, 2026: BigDiskBuster, which fills every byte of available disk space so Defender cannot install platform or signature updates, and which carries no CVE, no patch, and no Microsoft advisory.
topics.summary: A machine whose Defender cannot pull updates runs on stale detection while an attacker works. Administrators should monitor Defender update status, signature age, and free disk space across their fleets.

topics.summary: The FBI has confirmed neither the intrusion nor the PeopleSoft flaw, and Oracle has published no advisory for it. Home addresses and family details on federal agents expose them and their households to physical risk well beyond ordinary identity theft.

topics.title: Japan Dismantles Its First North Korean Laptop Farm
topics.latest_developments: Japanese authorities took down the country's first North Korean laptop farm, SecurityWeek reported on September 22, 2026, as the United States, Japan, Germany, and Australia published a joint report on the WaterPlum campaign that counts funds or credentials taken from more than 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets.
topics.summary: WaterPlum, the operation also tracked as Contagious Interview, poses as artificial intelligence and blockchain companies, recruits through fake job postings, and has infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries, moving $10.71 million in stolen cryptocurrency to North Korea. Web designers, engineers, and cryptocurrency specialists are the primary targets.

business_politics.summary: The average United States diesel price has climbed past $6.50 a gallon as the war with Iran and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries choke distillate supply worldwide. A ban would strand Gulf Coast cargoes that Europe and Latin America rely on, push the shortage onto foreign buyers, and reprice freight, farming, and heating costs six weeks before the midterm elections.

The speech ran campaign-style: he declared a "Golden Age of America," called international efforts to slow artificial intelligence a "globalist scheme," and suggested he could use further military force against America's neighbors. Iranian and Cuban delegates walked out during it.

Cheaper crude pulled buyers back into technology shares, carrying the Nasdaq 100 to a record, while United States natural gas futures jumped 4.5% to $2.965 per million British thermal units, their biggest one-day gain in six weeks. The diesel and inflation shock running through American prices hangs on whether the strait opens.

events.latest_developments: Wiz Khalifa told Pittsburgh City Paper in an interview published Tuesday, September 22, that he will open the Hill District's new venue, Citizens Live at The Wylie, on Friday, October 2, promising "lots of energy and a lot of weed smoke."
events.summary: The Pittsburgh rapper, who grew up in the city and broke through with "Black and Yellow," headlines the first show at Citizens Live at The Wylie, the new concert hall on Wylie Avenue in the Hill District.

sources.title: Wiz Khalifa is coming home to open Pittsburgh’s new Hill District venue

events.title: Backyard Docs Spreads Across Several Venues
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported Tuesday, September 22, that the Backyard Docs Film Festival, which started as a do-it-yourself backyard screening series, has grown into a multi-day event running at several Pittsburgh venues.
events.summary: This year's program takes up labor fights, immigration enforcement in the courts, a campaign to stop a pipeline, a fresh look at the East Palestine derailment, and a popular local haunt with a grim history.

sources.title: Backyard Docs has ballooned from DIY hangout to multi-day, multi-venue documentary destination

events.title: October Fills With Oktoberfests, Apples, and Giant Pumpkins
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its October food calendar Tuesday, September 22, listing Oktoberfest celebrations, apple harvest events, and giant pumpkin weigh-offs across the Pittsburgh region.
events.summary: Pittsburgh City Paper's food column the same morning reported that Oktoberfest season has opened around the city and that the Pleasure Bar has closed.

sources.title: Oktoberfest celebrations, apples, giant pumpkins and more food events in October
Oktoberfest kicks off, Pleasure Bar closes, and more Pittsburgh food news

around_teams.title: Footbahlin Digs Into 3.5 Yards a Play
around_teams.latest_developments: Ben Roethlisberger's Footbahlin posted episode 140 Tuesday evening, September 22, taking apart why the Steelers' offense looked stuck at New England.
around_teams.summary: Roethlisberger and the crew start with the offensive line, arguing that broken protection dries up the run game and turns third downs long, and they work through how Pittsburgh won time of possession while averaging 3.5 yards a play.

sources.title: Why The Steelers Offense Looked Stuck Against New England Ep. 140

around_teams.title: Hiles Lays the Roster at Omar Khan's Feet
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote Tuesday, September 22, that every one of the Steelers' biggest problems traces back to general manager Omar Khan.
around_teams.summary: Hiles spent the past two weeks arguing the offense lacks talent, and he now names the executive who assembled it. Khan built the 2026 roster around quarterback Aaron Rodgers and receiver DK Metcalf, both of whom drew poor Week 2 grades from the paper after the trip to Foxborough.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: All of the Steelers’ biggest problems are of GM Omar Khan’s making

around_teams.title: Doval Goes and Ashcraft Takes the Pitching Award
around_teams.latest_developments: The Pirates parted ways with reliever Camilo Doval Tuesday, September 22, and Pittsburgh's chapter of the Baseball Writers' Association of America the same day named right-hander Braxton Ashcraft the team's top pitcher over ace Paul Skenes, with Brandon Lowe taking most valuable player.
around_teams.summary: Doval came to Pittsburgh in a trade at the deadline, as did Lowe and outfielder Jake Mangum. Ashcraft's season ended Saturday, September 19, when the club put him on the injured list for the year, and Skenes has spoken publicly about the struggles that marked his 2026 and the part the World Baseball Classic played in them.

sources.title: The Pirates part ways with Camilo Doval, one of their trade deadline acquisitions
Braxton Ashcraft, not Paul Skenes, was named the Pirates' top pitcher by Pittsburgh's BBWAA chapter

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Takes Apart the Trip to Foxborough
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler returned to the Week 2 game on SNR Drive Tuesday, September 22, after rewatching it, brought in The Athletic's Mike DeFabo to open the show, went through the Steelers' snap counts player by player, and ran the league's Week 3 power rankings.
around_teams.summary: Monday's episode opened with first impressions of the offense and gave Steelers radio voice Rob King roughly 25 minutes on the air. The Steelers host the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium Sunday, September 27, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Recapping Steelers Vs. Patriots | SNR Drive (Sept.21) | Pittsburgh Steelers
Tuesday Rewind Thoughts + Week 3 Power Rankings | SNR Drive (Sept.22) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: Week 2 Grades Fall Hardest on Rodgers and the Line
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its Week 2 grades Tuesday morning, September 22, handing poor marks to quarterback Aaron Rodgers, receiver DK Metcalf, and the offensive line after the trip to New England.
around_teams.summary: The grades follow a week in which the Steelers' offense produced almost nothing at Gillette Stadium, head coach Mike McCarthy took the blame publicly, and the team began weighing changes up front, with rookie tackle Max Iheanachor in the conversation. Pittsburgh hosts the Cincinnati Bengals Sunday, September 27, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

sources.title: Steelers Week 2 grades: Poor marks for Aaron Rodgers and his supporting cast
The Steelers are contemplating changes on the offensive line after Sunday’s ugly showing

around_teams.title: Beazley Fields Pirates Questions
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette beat writer Colin Beazley held his Pirates chat Tuesday, September 22, taking reader questions with ace Paul Skenes among the subjects.
around_teams.summary: The chat follows the Pirates' elimination from playoff contention on Saturday, September 19, and Skenes' interview with the paper describing the struggles that marked his 2026 season and the part the World Baseball Classic played in them.

sources.title: Colin Beazley's Pirates chat transcript: 09.22.26

around_teams.title: Louis Lipps Cooks Louisiana Food on the North Shore
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled former Steelers receiver Louis Lipps on Tuesday, September 22, and printed the recipes he brings to his tailgate outside Acrisure Stadium.
around_teams.summary: Lipps, who grew up in Louisiana and caught passes for the Steelers from 1984 through 1991, feeds his tailgate crowd the food he was raised on before home games on the North Shore.

sources.title: A former Steeler brings some Louisiana sizzle to his Pittsburgh tailgate

team_usa.title: Pepi Calls His Injury a Minor Setback
team_usa.latest_developments: Ricardo Pepi said Tuesday, September 22, that the injury that took him out of PSV Eindhoven's match amounts to a "minor setback" and that his recovery has already begun.
team_usa.summary: The United States striker came off hurt Sunday, September 20, and Damion Downs took his place on Mauricio Pochettino's roster for four coming friendlies. Pepi aims to return to action with his club in the Netherlands.

sources.title: USMNT's Ricardo Pepi: Injury a 'minor setback'

team_usa.title: The USWNT Pipeline Draws Alarms
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN published an assessment Tuesday, September 22, asking whether the United States women's national team's grip on the world game is slipping as its youth sides keep losing.
team_usa.summary: The piece follows a run of poor results at the under-20 and under-17 levels, among them Brazil's penalty-shootout elimination of the United States in the round of 16 at the Under-20 Women's World Cup, and weighs how much of the alarm the numbers actually support.

sources.title: Is a lack of young talent putting the USWNT's world dominance at risk?

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Where're All The AI Chips?
reading.summary: Zitron goes looking for the graphics processors behind the industry's enormous reported capital spending and questions how much of that hardware has actually reached data centers and started earning revenue.

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: Amazon Blocks Muse, Amazon’s Moat, Aggregator v Aggregator
reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues Amazon's move to block the AI agent Muse was predictable, and that the two sides still have room to strike a deal because Amazon's warehouses, delivery network, and physical-world investments amount to a moat artificial intelligence cannot cross on its own.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport dismisses the notion that current systems lead to a superintelligence capable of killing billions, a claim Anthropic employees floated publicly, and argues that the race to build it does real damage regardless.
